The enterprise ecosystem router operates as a dynamic graph traversal mechanism across six distinct infrastructure layers—NVIDIA Inception, Developer, Sentry, PostHog, RunPod, and Google Cloud/Gemini—where routing decisions R_ij are made according to service availability and latency constraints. The continuous self-improving run loop functions as a feedback control system that logs empirical accuracy deltas ΔA_n against a reference model, updating internal parameters through iterative regression. The input harvesting distillation flywheel transforms heterogeneous agent-generated data streams into structured training sets E_k^SFT/DPO/GRPO, enabling downstream policy refinement. These three operators form a closed-loop architecture where telemetry from the run loop informs routing adjustments, which in turn influence the quality of distilled inputs. Dualities emerge between the router’s logical paths and the distillation process’s information flow; both exhibit modular compositionality under shared abstraction layers. Failure modes include routing deadlock when all services fail, stagnation in the run loop due to insufficient signal-to-noise ratio, and degradation in distillation fidelity from noisy or misaligned prompts.
